findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/checklist.ts:1347-1362 verification_evidence_refresh_stale rewrites stale evidence via makeEvidence() without copying evidence.mechanical / evidence.receipt / evidence.nonMechanicalReason (it only preserves verdict/waiverType/file/command/result/attestation/actorTrust/factProvenance). Empirically reproduced: record an audited non-mechanical escape (mechanical:false + nonMechanicalReason) against an executable (cli/logic/browser) intent -> buildVerificationCoverage correctly demotes it to status=non_mechanical (blocking, missingRequired=1). Advance HEAD so the evidence goes stale (normal after any further commit). Call verification_evidence_refresh_stale (the documented `done_prepare --refreshStale` path per CLAUDE.md DONE convergence guidance) -> the rewritten evidence row has mechanical=undefined, nonMechanicalReason=undefined, receipt=undefined. Re-running buildVerificationCoverage at the same head now returns status=covered, missingRequired=0 -- the audited non-mechanical escape silently gets promoted to full coverage with zero re-execution. This directly reopens the gate bypass that CHK-004s adversarial verificationIntent claims is closed (recording an executable intent as type:manual cannot bypass execution at the coverage gate, the escape hatch is closed) and is a NEW gap introduced by this stors mechanical/non_mechanical distinction (pre-B-ec67 there was no tiered trust to launder). Modifying verification_evidence_refresh_stale itself is explicitly out of scope per scope-check.json (owned by B-3b88 per decision.json/understanding.json), so this is not a scope violation by the implementer, but the resulting live bypass is real, reachable via a routine documented operation, and undocumented as a residual risk anywhere in this stors artifacts. Same silent field-drop also destroys mechanical:true receipts (exitCode/outputDigest/outputTail/executedAt all lost on refresh) though that case does not flip the status. Recommend: either (a) have refresh_stale copy forward ev.mechanical/ev.receipt/ev.nonMechanicalReason unchanged (narrow, does not change what gets re-certified, just stops dropping already-recorded fields), or (b) add an explicit handoff/scope note for B-3b88 flagging this exact reachable bypass so it is not silently inherited.

CHK-003:edge:0 (must) overclaims: evidence note says the smoke asserts outputDigest == sha256(captured output) and outputTail is bounded, but tool-executed-evidence-receipt-smoke.ts:114 only regex-checks the digest looks like a 64-hex string (/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/) and never recomputes sha256 of the actual captured output to compare equality; no test ever produces output longer than VERIFICATION_OUTPUT_TAIL_CHARS (4000, checklist.ts:308) to prove outputTail is actually truncated/bounded rather than just full output. Demonstrated by mutation: patched dist/handlers/checklist.js sha256Hex(value) (src checklist.ts:311-313) to hash a constant wrong string instead of run.output, then reran node packages/main/dist/tasks/tool-executed-evidence-receipt-smoke.js — it still printed PASS/exit 0. A broken digest computation (or truncation bound) would go undetected by this must-intent evidence.

CHK-003:happy:0 (must) overclaims "the result field is derived from the actual exit code, not the caller": in every smoke case where caller-claimed result and actual exit could differ, checklist.ts:482-486 THROWS (refuses the whole write) rather than storing an overridden value, so no test ever proves derivation vs echoing the caller — a case where caller under-claims or omits result (e.g. result omitted/'fail' while exit==0 and selector matches) succeeds without throwing and derivedResult (checklist.ts:502,505) silently overrides, but this path is never exercised. Demonstrated by mutation: changed checklist.js line `result: derivedResult,` to `result: input.result ?? derivedResult,` (i.e. echo caller when supplied) and reran the smoke — still PASS/exit 0, because all passing smoke calls pass result:'pass' matching the true outcome. The must-intent claim of tool-derived (not caller-derived) result is therefore unverified for the only case that would distinguish it.

CHK-004:happy:0 (must) overclaims "manual|docs evidence is stored as attestation, marked explicitly non-mechanical, with no command execution attempted": the smoke never calls verification_evidence_add/batch_add against an intent whose type is literally 'manual' or 'docs' (the genuine attestation-only branch at checklist.ts:400-409, `if (!isExecutableIntentType(intent.type))`). The only 'manual' coverage in the smoke is (a) block 7a which uses kind:manual_transcript against an intent of type 'cli' (an EXECUTABLE type) via the separate audited-escape branch (checklist.ts:413-428), and (b) block 7c which calls buildVerificationCoverage directly on a hand-built fixture, bypassing the handler entirely. Demonstrated by mutation: changed `if (!isExecutableIntentType(intent.type))` to `if (false)` in dist/handlers/checklist.js, disabling the entire attestation-only branch, and reran the smoke — still PASS/exit 0. The actual handler code path for a genuinely manual/docs-typed intent is exercised by zero assertions in this smoke despite being claimed as covered.

CHK-005:edge:0/adversarial:0 (must) overclaim per CLAUDE.md handler convention (Zod min/max must be re-validated at handler entry AND tested via a bypass path): command-catalog.ts:465,480 Zod-enforce nonMechanicalReason.min(30); checklist.ts:309 MIN_NON_MECHANICAL_ESCAPE_REASON=30 re-validates it at handler entry (checklist.ts:414-419, throws non_mechanical_reason_too_short) — matching the convention. But no smoke case ever exercises a sub-30-char nonMechanicalReason through the internal fn-call path (env.handlers.verification_evidence_add bypasses Zod entirely already); the smoke only uses one long reason string (line 264, ~78 chars). Demonstrated by mutation: changed `const MIN_NON_MECHANICAL_ESCAPE_REASON = 30;` to `= 0;` in dist/handlers/checklist.js (fully disabling the runtime re-validation this checklist item exists to guarantee) and reran the smoke — still PASS/exit 0. This is exactly the F-005/F-006/F-019 pattern CLAUDE.md calls out: a runtime constraint with zero test proving the bypass path is still enforced.
